title: Explain earlier causes and solve past problems
lessons:
## Communication goal
Explain not only what happened, but what had already happened before it. Reconstruct a problem from messages, distinguish a cause from a later response, and propose a useful next step. This chapter closes the past-narration phase; its tasks integrate Chapters 9–11 rather than replacing them.

## Prerequisites and diagnostic
You need passé composé auxiliary selection and participles, imparfait endings, and a simple sequence with first/then/finally. Retrieve these aloud: `J'ai perdu mon billet.` — I lost my ticket. `Je cherchais mon billet.` — I was looking for my ticket. The first presents an event, the second an ongoing scene. If you cannot form either, review Chapters 10–11 before adding the earlier-past relationship. You do not need an English tense label to understand a timeline.

## 1. Form an earlier past
The plus-que-parfait uses imparfait avoir or être plus the past participle. Avoir forms: `j'avais, tu avais, il avait, nous avions, vous aviez, elles avaient`. Être forms: `j'étais, tu étais, elle était, nous étions, vous étiez, ils étaient`. Add the same participle you use in passé composé: `J'avais envoyé le dossier.` — I had sent the file. `Elle était partie.` — She had left. `Nous nous étions inscrits.` — We had registered. No new participle set is needed, but retrieve irregulars: fait — done, pris — taken, vu — seen, reçu — received, écrit — written, mis — put, dû — had to, ouvert — opened, été — been, eu — had. `J'avais dû annuler.` — I had had to cancel.

Choose the auxiliary by the same construction as Chapter 10: `Il avait sorti les cartons.` — He had taken the boxes out. `Il était sorti.` — He had gone out. With ordinary être verbs, agree with the subject: `Les invitées étaient arrivées.` — The female guests had arrived. With avoir, agree with a preceding direct object, not the subject: `Les places que j'avais réservées étaient au balcon.` — The seats I had booked were in the balcony. With pronominals, retain the object distinction: `Elle s'était préparée.` — She had got ready; `Elle s'était lavé les mains.` — She had washed her hands; `Ils s'étaient téléphoné.` — They had phoned each other. Do not let the longer tense hide familiar agreement rules.

## 2. Find the reference point
The plus-que-parfait places one action before another past reference point. `Quand je suis arrivé, le guichet avait fermé.` — When I arrived, the counter had closed. Counter closing comes first; arrival is the later viewpoint. Compare `Quand je suis arrivé, le guichet a fermé.` — When I arrived, the counter closed: closing occurs at that point in the story. And `Quand je suis arrivé, le guichet était fermé.` — When I arrived, the counter was closed: this describes a state, without directly narrating the closing action.

You can combine all three tenses: `Je cherchais mon téléphone, mais je l'avais laissé au bureau. J'ai donc appelé un collègue.` — I was looking for my phone, but I had left it at the office. So I called a colleague. Cherchais gives background; avais laissé explains the earlier cause; ai appelé moves the story forward. Do not use plus-que-parfait for every old event. If you tell events in their actual order, passé composé can be enough: `J'ai réservé, puis j'ai payé.` — I booked, then paid. If you start from the later problem, earlier background becomes useful: `Le site a refusé mon paiement parce que j'avais saisi un mauvais numéro.` — The site rejected my payment because I had entered a wrong number.

## 3. Negation, questions and useful markers
Negation surrounds the auxiliary: `Je n'avais pas reçu le rappel.` — I had not received the reminder. With a reflexive pronoun: `Elle ne s'était pas réveillée.` — She had not woken up. Common adverbs go between auxiliary and participle: `Ils avaient déjà quitté les lieux.` — They had already left the premises. `Nous n'avions jamais utilisé cette application.` — We had never used this application. Ask `Aviez-vous vérifié la date ?` — Had you checked the date? or `Est-ce que vous aviez vérifié la date ?` — Had you checked the date?

Useful markers include déjà — already, auparavant — beforehand, la veille — the day before, jusque-là — until then, and après coup — afterwards/on reflection. `La veille, j'avais changé d'adresse.` — The day before, I had changed address. La veille is relative to a day in the story, not necessarily yesterday. A tense is not selected by a marker alone: identify what happened before what.

## 4. Explain fairly, not just blame
Separate a fact, a likely cause and a request. `Le document ne s'ouvrait pas. Vous l'aviez peut-être enregistré dans un autre format. Pourriez-vous le renvoyer ?` — The document would not open. Perhaps you had saved it in another format. Could you send it again? The last request is a useful polite chunk; Chapter 14 teaches its form. `D'après le reçu…` — According to the receipt… and `il semble que…` — it seems that… help avoid unsupported blame, but use only structures you can control. Prefer a clear factual sentence over a complicated accusation. English traps: I had a problem is usually `J'avais un problème.` — a background state, or `J'ai eu un problème.` — a completed incident, not automatically plus-que-parfait. Had to is obligation; had done is anteriority. `J'avais dû attendre.` — I had had to wait, contains both.

## 5. Hear relationships
The auxiliary carries time: `j'ai envoyé` — I sent, `j'avais envoyé` — I had sent. Listen for avais, not just the final participle. In `ils avaient déjà payé`, the final participle is the same as in passé composé. Written gender/number agreement is often silent. Pronounce the full chunk, then use it in a two-event explanation without reading. Browser voices are synthetic; replay can support learning but cannot establish readiness for natural exam audio. If audio fails, retry and keep text comprehension separate.

## 6. Attempt and reveal
A. Put the earlier closure before my arrival. B. Explain that the reminder never arrived before the missed appointment. C. Contrast she had gone upstairs and she had carried the suitcase upstairs. D. Retell a problem with scene, earlier cause and response.

:::answer
A. `Le bureau avait fermé quand je suis arrivé.` — The office had closed when I arrived, said by a male speaker. B. `J'ai manqué le rendez-vous parce que je n'avais pas reçu le rappel.` — I missed the appointment because I had not received the reminder. C. `Elle était montée. Elle avait monté la valise.` — She had gone upstairs. She had carried the suitcase upstairs. D. Example: `Je cherchais la salle. Le service avait changé le lieu sans me prévenir. J'ai appelé l'accueil.` — I was looking for the room. The department had changed the venue without telling me. I called reception. Other coherent timelines are valid.
:::

## 7. Four-skill synthesis and spacing
Before listening, draw earlier/later columns. After listening, reconstruct the sequence from memory before seeing the script. Read evidence and distinguish explicit facts from assumptions. For speaking and writing, include one earlier cause only where useful; no tense quota should distort the message. Recycle comparisons to choose a remedy, questions to clarify, and past narration for the complaint. Work through four bank groups of 25. A four-hour session can allocate 35 minutes recall, 45 listening, 40 reading, 45 speaking, 45 writing and 30 error review. Revisit after one day, three days, seven days and two weeks. If timelines fail, draw them with three events before conjugating. If forms fail, practise one auxiliary/participle pair in a meaningful sentence. End this phase with a fresh four-skill attempt; record weak abilities separately. Chapter completion is not an NCLC result.

activities.title: Why the parcel went elsewhere
activities.prompt: What earlier action explains the failed delivery?
activities.script: J'attendais un colis jeudi. Le suivi indiquait une livraison réussie, mais je n'avais rien reçu. J'ai appelé le transporteur. Nous avons découvert que j'avais conservé mon ancienne adresse dans mon compte. Le livreur avait donc déposé le colis chez mon ancien voisin. Heureusement, ce voisin l'a gardé et j'ai pu le récupérer.
options: The customer had kept an old address in the account.
The transport company had cancelled the order.
activities.explanation: The outdated saved address precedes and explains delivery to the former neighbour. The parcel was kept and later collected, not lost or refused.

activities.title: A room change
activities.script: Hier, notre réunion a commencé en retard. Nous cherchions la salle habituelle, mais elle était fermée. La veille, une fuite avait abîmé le plafond. Le secrétariat avait envoyé un message le matin, mais personne dans notre équipe ne l'avait lu. Après un appel à l'accueil, nous avons trouvé la nouvelle salle.
options: The team found the new room.
activities.explanation: The leak occurred the previous day, before the message, search, call and delayed meeting. Plus-que-parfait and la veille establish the earlier cause.

activities.title: A payment timeline
activities.passage: Le 4 novembre, j'ai réglé ma facture en ligne. Comme je n'avais pas reçu de confirmation, j'ai recommencé le paiement le lendemain. Le service a ensuite constaté deux débits. La première opération avait pourtant réussi : le message de confirmation avait été envoyé dans mon dossier indésirable. Un remboursement est maintenant en cours.
options: The shop had charged a late fee.
The customer had received two separate invoices.
A successful first payment had gone unconfirmed in the customer's inbox.
activities.explanation: The first transaction succeeded but its confirmation went to spam. Believing it had not succeeded, the customer paid again.

activities.title: An incident report
activities.prompt: Which statement is established, rather than merely possible?
activities.passage: À mon arrivée, la porte du local était ouverte. Le gardien avait quitté le bâtiment à dix-huit heures, après avoir fermé les fenêtres. Je n'ai pas vu qui avait ouvert la porte. Une équipe de nettoyage était peut-être passée. J'ai signalé la situation et attendu le responsable sans entrer.
options: The narrator found an open door and reported it.
The caretaker had left all the windows open.
The cleaning team certainly opened the door.
The narrator entered and searched the room.
activities.explanation: The open door, report and waiting are explicit facts. The cleaning team's visit is only a possibility; nobody is identified as the person who opened the door.

activities.title: Reconstruct a service problem
activities.prompt: Invent a missed appointment caused by an earlier administrative mistake. Explain the scene, the mistake, how you discovered it, and your requested solution. Then respond to the imagined challenge: Our system shows a confirmation. Ask a clarifying question rather than simply repeating yourself.
activities.model: Bonjour, je suis arrivé pour mon rendez-vous de dix heures, mais mon nom n'était pas sur la liste. J'avais réservé par téléphone lundi et votre collègue m'avait donné ce créneau. À l'accueil, nous avons découvert que la réservation avait été enregistrée pour la semaine suivante. Je comprends que votre système affiche une confirmation. Pouvez-vous vérifier la date de cette confirmation et l'adresse utilisée ? J'ai gardé le message reçu lundi. Comme j'ai déjà pris congé aujourd'hui, je demande un rendez-vous cet après-midi si une place est disponible.
rubric: Fulfillment: identifies scene, earlier cause, discovery and remedy.
Interaction: responds to the challenge with a relevant clarification.
Coherence: separates earlier mistake from later discovery.
Control/range: uses all three past tenses where meaningful, without forcing them.
Intelligibility/register: polite, evidence-based explanation rather than unsupported blame.

activities.title: Explain and repair a misunderstanding
activities.prompt: Write 110–150 words to a community organizer after an invented event problem. Explain an earlier cause, distinguish confirmed facts from an assumption, describe your response and propose prevention. Learning task, not official exam scoring.
activities.model:
Bonjour Madame,
Je vous écris au sujet de l'atelier de samedi. À mon arrivée, la salle était fermée et plusieurs participants attendaient dehors. J'avais consulté le programme imprimé la semaine précédente, qui indiquait cette adresse. Après un appel, nous avons appris que le lieu avait changé. Je n'avais pas reçu le message de modification ; il est peut-être arrivé dans mon dossier indésirable, mais je ne peux pas le confirmer. Nous avons finalement rejoint le groupe avec trente minutes de retard. Pour éviter ce problème, je propose d'afficher un avis à l'ancienne entrée et de demander une confirmation de lecture lors d'un changement important. Merci pour l'accueil de votre équipe malgré notre retard.
Cordialement,
Maya
rubric: Fulfillment: explains earlier cause, evidence, response and prevention.
Coherence: timeline and causal relationship are clear.
Range: combines narrative, cautious explanation and proposal.
Control: auxiliary, participles, agreement and negation are checked.
Register: constructive and polite; assumptions are not presented as facts.
